questions.stem: The founder of the Mughal Empire in India, Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur, defeated Ibrahim Lodi in which decisive battle?
questions.explanation: FIRST BATTLE OF PANIPAT (21 April 1526): Babur's 12,000 troops defeated Ibrahim Lodi's 100,000 with superior artillery (early gunpowder/cannons) and the TULUGHMA battle formation. Ibrahim Lodi was killed — the ONLY Delhi Sultan to die on the battlefield. This founded the Mughal Empire. Later Babur-era battles: KHANWA (1527, defeated Rana Sanga of Mewar), CHANDERI (1528, Medini Rai), GHAGHRA (1529, Afghans + Bengal sultan). Babur wrote Babur-nama (autobiography in Turkish/Chagatai).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Humayun was defeated by which Afghan ruler, forcing him to flee India for 15 years?
questions.explanation: SHER SHAH SURI (born Farid Khan, 1486–1545) defeated Humayun at the BATTLE OF CHAUSA (1539) and then decisively at the BATTLE OF KANNAUJ / BILGRAM (1540). Humayun fled to Persia (Safavid court of Shah Tahmasp) for 15 years. Sher Shah ruled 1540-45 and founded the SUR DYNASTY. Sher Shah's reforms: Grand Trunk Road extension (Sonargaon to Peshawar), silver RUPIYA coin (basis of modern rupee), postal system, land revenue (zabt system — precursor to Akbar's reforms), sarais. Died in cannon explosion at Kalinjar 1545. Humayun regained Delhi in 1555 but died falling down stairs in 1556 — 'Humayun tumbled through life and tumbled out of it'.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Akbar came to the throne at what age, and who was his regent during the early years?
questions.explanation: Akbar (Jalal-ud-din Muhammad Akbar, born 1542, Umarkot) ascended the throne in 1556 at age 13 after Humayun's death. His regent/guardian for the first 4 years was BAIRAM KHAN (Turkoman noble, father of Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan). Akbar's first major victory: SECOND BATTLE OF PANIPAT (5 Nov 1556) — Bairam Khan led Mughal forces against HEMU (the Hindu Suri-era general who had briefly captured Delhi). Bairam's regency ended in 1560 (dismissed by Akbar's foster-mother Maham Anaga). Akbar ruled till 1605 (49 years — longest-reigning Mughal).

questions.stem: The MANSABDARI system — Akbar's military-administrative framework — was based on:

options.option_text: DUAL RANKS: zat (personal status) and sawar
Fixed cash salaries for all nobles

questions.explanation: MANSABDARI (Persian 'mansab' = rank) was Akbar's systematic bureaucracy. Each mansabdar had TWO ranks: ZAT (personal status and pay — from 10 to 5000, later up to 10,000 for imperial family) and SAWAR (number of cavalrymen he must maintain — couldn't exceed zat). Rewards were in CASH SALARIES or JAGIRS (revenue assignments — NOT hereditary territorial grants; transferable). Three categories: TROOPED, DUSPA (half on duty), SIHPA. Disadvantages: became corrupt/inefficient over time, led to Mughal decline. Introduced ~1575 following Central Asian precedent. cavalry obligation.
questions.subject: History

_fixes.was: DUAL RANKS: zat (personal status) and sawar (cavalry obligation)
_fixes.now: DUAL RANKS: zat (personal status) and sawar

questions.stem: Akbar's 'NAVARATNA' (Nine Gems) at court included which of the following?

options.option_text: Tansen, Birbal, Todar Mal, Abul Fazl, Faizi, Raja Man Singh, Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, Mullah Do-Piyaza, Fakir Aziao-Din
Tansen, Kalidasa, Varahamihira, Aryabhata (those are Gupta-era gems)
Tansen, Mirza Ghalib, Sir Syed Ahmed Khan (those are 19th c. figures)

questions.explanation: The Nine Gems at Akbar's court (per later Mughal legend): (1) TANSEN — musician, raga-inventor (Miyan ki Todi, Darbari Kanada); (2) BIRBAL (Mahesh Das) — wit + advisor, died Yusufzai campaign 1586; (3) TODAR MAL — finance minister, land revenue reforms (DAHSALA system — zabt); (4) ABUL FAZL — chronicler, wrote AIN-I-AKBARI + AKBARNAMA in Persian; assassinated 1602 on Prince Salim's orders; (5) FAIZI — poet, Abul Fazl's brother; (6) RAJA MAN SINGH — Rajput general (Amer/Jaipur), subjugated Bengal and Orissa; (7) ABDUR RAHIM KHAN-I-KHANAN — poet, translated Babur-nama into Persian, son of Bairam Khan; (8) MULLAH DO-PIYAZA; (9) FAKIR AZIAO-DIN. 'Navratna' at Chandragupta II's court is a different/earlier tradition.

questions.stem: Akbar's new syncretic religion 'DIN-I-ILAHI' was proclaimed in which year?
questions.explanation: DIN-I-ILAHI ('Divine Faith') was proclaimed by Akbar in 1582 — a syncretic creed borrowing from Islam, Hinduism, Zoroastrianism, Jainism, Christianity. Prior steps: 1575 IBADAT KHANA (House of Worship) at Fatehpur Sikri for religious debates; 1579 MAZHAR (Infallibility Decree) making Akbar the final arbiter on religious disputes. Din-i-Ilahi had ~19 followers (Birbal being the most prominent) — it died with Akbar. Most orthodox Muslims (including Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi) rejected it. Other Akbar religious policies: abolished JIZYA 1564 (re-imposed by Aurangzeb), PILGRIM TAX abolished 1563, allowed inter-faith marriages (married Rajput princess — later queen mother Mariam-uz-Zamani, Jodha Bai).

questions.stem: The BATTLE OF HALDIGHATI (1576) was fought between the Mughal forces (led by Raja Man Singh) and which Rajput king?
questions.explanation: BATTLE OF HALDIGHATI (18 June 1576, in the Aravalli foothills near Kumbhalgarh, Rajasthan). Mughal forces led by RAJA MAN SINGH (not Akbar personally) vs MAHARANA PRATAP of Mewar (with Afghan general Hakim Khan Sur + Bhil tribal archers). TACTICAL Mughal victory, STRATEGIC stalemate — Rana Pratap escaped on his legendary horse CHETAK (who carried him to safety despite a fatal wound). Rana Pratap continued guerrilla resistance from Aravalli hills, reclaimed most of Mewar by 1585. Rana Pratap's story is a symbol of Rajput resistance; his death 1597. Rana Sanga (different king) had fought Babur at Khanwa 1527.

questions.stem: Akbar shifted his capital FROM Agra TO Fatehpur Sikri in which year, and for what reason?

options.option_text: 1571; to honour Sufi saint Shaikh Salim Chishti who blessed him with a son
1605; to be closer to the Deccan frontier

questions.explanation: Akbar shifted his capital to FATEHPUR SIKRI in 1571 to commemorate SHAIKH SALIM CHISHTI's prophecy that he would have a son (who became Jahangir, born 1569). Fatehpur Sikri ('City of Victory') housed the BULAND DARWAZA (1576, commemorating Gujarat conquest — tallest gateway in the world, 54m), the TOMB of Salim Chishti, the DIWAN-I-KHAS (private audience hall), JAMA MASJID, PANCH MAHAL (5-story pleasure palace), IBADAT KHANA. Capital abandoned by 1585 due to water shortage; Akbar moved to Lahore till 1598, then back to Agra. UNESCO WHS since 1986.

questions.stem: The DAHSALA (Ten-Year) land revenue system was introduced under Akbar by which minister?
questions.explanation: DAHSALA ZABT system (introduced 1580) — designed by RAJA TODAR MAL, Akbar's finance minister. Method: surveyed cultivated land, categorised by productivity (POLAJ — always cultivated, PARAUTI — left fallow, CHACHAR — 3-4 years fallow, BANJAR — 5+ years fallow), averaged yields of last 10 years, fixed 1/3 of produce as state share (payable in cash or kind based on prevailing prices). Applied in Northern India — Punjab, Allahabad, Awadh, Delhi, Agra, Bihar, Ajmer, Malwa, Lahore, Multan. Todar Mal also conducted comprehensive surveys in BIHAR and BENGAL. Earlier under Sher Shah, he'd served as revenue commissioner. Died 1589. Land revenue system was the single most important administrative innovation — lasted (with modifications) till the British.

questions.stem: Humayun's Tomb in Delhi, built after his death in 1556, was commissioned by:
questions.explanation: HUMAYUN'S TOMB (1565–72), Delhi — commissioned by Humayun's widow HAMIDA BANU BEGUM (a.k.a. Haji Begum). Architect: Mirak Mirza Ghiyath (Persian). It's the FIRST GARDEN-TOMB on the Indian subcontinent and an architectural precursor to the TAJ MAHAL (90 years later, 1632-53, built by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal). Features: Persian-style CHAR BAGH garden (quadrilateral), double-dome, red sandstone + white marble inlays, axial symmetry. UNESCO WHS since 1993. Humayun's body was originally in Purana Qila; Hamida moved it here. Several later Mughals were also interred here (Dara Shikoh, Rahim Khan-i-Khanan). Library (Sher Mandal) at Purana Qila is where Humayun fell to his death (1556). Humayun's widow, mother of Akbar.
questions.subject: History

_fixes.was: Hamida Banu Begum (Humayun's widow, mother of Akbar)
